solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Trade fair certain to be feared by crooks

parts.note: an expo is a large trade exhibition
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A trade show that swindlers would rather stay away from because they are bound to be caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooks dread being publicly revealed, so being found out is what they fear most.

clue.text: Allow what would be rational without its head

indicators.note: without its head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a reasonable position that can be defended is tenable

explanation.surface: Permit what would make sense if it lost its leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something possible or permit it is a straightforward synonym for allow.

clue.text: Opera star flips out — white powder implicated

indicators.note: flips out suggests the letters going wild and being thrown into a new order
implicated, meaning folded in or entangled, reinforces the mixing up of the letters

explanation.surface: A singer loses control and drugs are suspected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white powder' suggests cocaine in a scandal; it is the gypsum powder used for casts and moulds.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a white gypsum powder that sets hard when mixed with water, used for casts and moulds.

clue.text: Sensible sounding flower seen at 24

indicators.note: sounding means the word is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: sensible means sane

explanation.surface: A practical-seeming bloom found in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower is crossword code for river, a thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, and this French river runs through the capital named at 24.

clue.text: Astonish everyone in a tiny remote island

parts.note: to rock someone is to shock or astonish them
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Amaze everybody on a far-flung little island.
explanation.definitionFit: This uninhabited granite islet in the North Atlantic, west of Scotland, is famously small and isolated.

clue.text: Substitute not quite satisfying hunger

indicators.note: not quite means the word is left one letter short of complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: food that is satisfying the hunger is filling

explanation.surface: A stand-in meal that doesn't entirely fill you up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in who temporarily takes another person's place is a common noun synonym for a substitute.

clue.text: I'm on time at university, yet unprepared

parts.note: being on time means being prompt

explanation.surface: A student boasts of punctuality while admitting to having done no preparation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done off the cuff, with no rehearsal, is spontaneous and unprepared.

clue.text: Places to hide from landlords when penniless

indicators.note: penniless means losing the old penny, abbreviated D in pre-decimal British money

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landowner

explanation.surface: Somewhere to dodge the landlords when you can't pay the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal's den, where it rests and hides, is the sense here.

clue.text: Prototypal wildlife refuge

parts.note: the biblical vessel that saved pairs of animals from the Flood was the first animal sanctuary

explanation.surface: The original nature reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the vessel built before the Flood sheltered every kind of creature, the first refuge for wildlife.

clue.text: A measure to contain strike in an emergency

indicators.note: to contain means the measure wraps around the word for a strike

parts.note: an inch is a measure of length
to tap is to strike lightly

explanation.surface: A dose of something to hold off a blow when things go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means if absolutely necessary, as one might do when an urgent crisis forces it.

clue.text: The best things to choose with first-class degree

parts.note: to opt is to choose
first class is I, the Roman numeral one, as in a first
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Picking the top options when you hold a first-class degree.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Latin plural of the word for the most favourable outcome or condition.

clue.text: Your setter needs a second reminder

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
mo is short for moment, a second

explanation.surface: The puzzle compiler needs another prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like 'another' but means a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written note jotted to prompt the memory is a reminder.

clue.text: The Mill at Henley is partly Turner's work

indicators.note: is partly means only part of the phrase about the mill is used, the letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A painting of a mill at the Thames town of Henley attributed to the artist J. M. W. Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter, but here it is a woodturner, whose work is done at this machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodturner shapes material while it spins on this machine tool, so it is where a turner works.

clue.text: A dreadful hole employs old boozers

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters are in a terrible state and need rearranging

parts.note: to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: An awful dump that still uses old drunks.
explanation.walkthrough: Boozer is British slang for a pub, so 'old boozers' are old pubs, not elderly drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Taverns selling beer were once commonly known by this name, an old term for pubs.

clue.text: Dangerous for Yorkshire folk but you can bear it

indicators.note: Yorkshire speech is stereotyped as dropping the letter H at the start of words

parts.note: dangerous means harmful

explanation.surface: Something that is a hazard to people from Yorkshire, but which you can tolerate.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is a county in northern England whose accent is said to drop initial H. 'bear' means carry, not put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount carried in the arms is exactly what a person can bear, meaning carry.

clue.text: Legal tender? Not a bit of it!

definitions.text: Legal tender? Not a bit of it!

parts.words: Legal tender? Not a bit of it!
parts.note: a bit is also a coin, so a counterfeit one is certainly not legal tender

explanation.surface: A scornful denial that something is lawful currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' plays on the old coins called threepenny and sixpenny bits.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterfeit piece of money is the opposite of legal currency, a forged bit.

clue.text: It could be written down in theory

definitions.meaning: something set down in writing exists on the page
an idea that works in principle rather than in practice

explanation.surface: A plan that could be recorded in writing but may only work hypothetically.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes something written on a sheet, and idiomatically means theoretically.

clue.text: A simple falling-out with the defendant? On the contrary

parts.note: simple means plain
a tiff is a small quarrel or falling-out

explanation.surface: A minor dispute with the accused, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: In a lawsuit the person bringing the case is the opposite party to the one being sued.

clue.text: Some steps outside an upper window

indicators.note: outside means the steps go around the short word

parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs

explanation.surface: Stairs outside leading up to a window high on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A small window set above a door, often semicircular with radiating bars, sits high up.

clue.text: Twin boys arrive initially in Lucerne

indicators.note: twin means the boy's name appears as a pair

parts.note: Alf is a boy's name, short for Alfred

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of arrive

explanation.surface: Two brothers turn up in the Swiss city of Lucerne.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucerne looks like the Swiss city, but it is another name for a fodder plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is the British name for the forage plant that Americans know by this other name.

clue.text: Puts on assorted dishes Delia suggests, for starters

indicators.note: for starters means take the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A cook serves a variety of dishes recommended by Delia Smith, as first courses.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is a famous British TV cookery writer.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something on top or include it is to append or add it.

clue.text: Outlaw takes refuge in mountain country

indicators.note: takes means the word for outlaw holds the shelter inside it

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
a hut is a simple shelter or refuge

explanation.surface: A fugitive hides out somewhere in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: This Himalayan kingdom is a famously mountainous nation between India and China.

clue.text: A pub has to profit by a good deal

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to profit is to gain

explanation.surface: A pub needs to make money by giving value.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchase at a low price, offering good value, is a bargain.

clue.text: Not familiar with the meaning of pristine

definitions.meaning: a person not accustomed to something is not used to it
pristine means in original, untouched condition

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't know what a word for spotless means.
explanation.definitionFit: Followed by 'to' the word means not accustomed; alone it means never handled, like new.

clue.text: Boss keeps a PR who can understand speech

indicators.note: keeps means the boss holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a boss is a leader
a means one, which is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A manager employs a public relations person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows talk by watching the speaker's mouth can understand speech without hearing it.

clue.text: See 2
Saw a danger for funambulists going backwards

indicators.note: going backwards means the phrase about the danger is read in reverse

parts.note: funambulists are tightrope walkers, for whom having no net beneath them is a danger

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a hazard for tightrope walkers as they moved in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see; it is the tool, as in a tenon saw, used to cut joints.
explanation.definitionFit: This word names a fine-toothed backsaw used by carpenters to cut joints, so it stands for that saw.

clue.text: It goes up on the tenth

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second
in a down clue goes up means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Something that rises on the tenth day of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a tenth of produce or income paid to the Church was called this, so it is a tenth.

clue.text: Monster cheese a French writer avoided

indicators.note: avoided means the writer is left out of the cheese

parts.note: Gorgonzola is an Italian blue cheese
Emile Zola was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A monstrous cheese that a French author steered clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa and her sisters were snake-haired monsters in Greek myth.

clue.text: Army or Navy officers of unequal rank, oddly

definitions.text: Army or Navy officers of unequal rank, oddly

parts.words: Army or Navy officers of unequal rank, oddly
parts.note: the same title is borne by officers in both services, but a naval one ranks well above an army one

explanation.surface: Military officers from two services who strangely hold different grades.
explanation.walkthrough: An army holder of this title equals a navy lieutenant, while a navy holder equals an army colonel.
explanation.definitionFit: The single title names officers in both services, yet the naval rank is senior to the army rank.

clue.text: It's possibly an English drink such as camomile tea

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Perhaps an English drink like camomile tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges IT'S into TIS; AN and E follow unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion of herbs, of which camomile is a classic example, is a herbal tea.

clue.text: Friend due to run wild without one, like Oliver Twist?

indicators.note: to run wild means the letters of the two words are jumbled
without means one letter is taken away from the jumble

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A friend about to go wild, missing someone, like Dickens's orphan.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of FRIEND DUE, less I, are rearranged. Oliver Twist is Dickens's workhouse orphan who famously asks for more food.
explanation.definitionFit: The workhouse boy was given too little to eat, so he was hungry and poorly nourished; the question mark marks an example.
